[Highway Networks](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.00387) use y=T(h)⊙H(h)+(1−T(h))⊙h, with T=σ(Wh+b), typically initialized with negative biases to favor carrying h. Setting H(h)=h+u gives y=h+T(h)⊙u: residual gating is already implicit in highways. [TFT’s Gated Residual Network](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2021.03.012) explicitly uses LayerNorm(h+σ(Wgη+bg)⊙(Wvη+bv)), with optional context entering η. Thus input-dependent channelwise residual gating has clear precedents; conditioning directly on [h;u] and the particular initialization are narrower distinctions.

For the proposed y=h+[σ(W[h;u]+b)/σ(2)]⊙u, W=0 and b=2 give exactly h+u at initialization, preserving the ungated residual block rather than approximating identity. Algebraically, the multiplier lies in (0,1.1353), allowing suppression and modest amplification; its initial logit derivative is 1−σ(2)≈0.1192. The constant denominator can be absorbed into a freely scalable residual branch, so it primarily specifies initialization/optimization rather than a new function class. [Savarese and Figueiredo’s Residual Gates](https://home.ttic.edu/~savarese/savarese_files/Residual_Gates.pdf) already study h+g(k)u with a learned, input-independent scalar per block and report improvements over ungated networks—evidence that static scaling alone can help.

Recommended controls, derived from these comparisons: fixed multiplier 1; learned blockwise scalar; learned channelwise bias-only σ(b)/σ(2), initialized at b=2; and the full contextual gate. Keep backbone, branch initialization and training identical. Compare h-only, u-only and [h;u] conditioning. Bias-only versus contextual gating isolates input dependence from channel scaling. Highway gate visualizations demonstrate varying activity, but do not substitute for this controlled comparison.
